task: Correct grammar errors throughout this fictional three-paragraph breach-remedies section. Preserve all remedy types, the cure provision, the election mechanism, and the damages limitation exactly. Do not add or remove remedies, change the notice period, or alter any substantive obligation.
input:
In the event of a material breach, the non-breaching party may terminating the agreement upon 30 days written notice and pursuing damages in accordance with Clause 12. Injunctive relief are available without the notice requirement.

Where the breaching party remedies the breach within 15 days of the written notice, the non-breaching party may elects to continue the agreement on its existing terms. The election to continue do not constitute a waiver of the non-breaching party's right to claim damages for loss suffered during the period of breach.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party may pursuing claims for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages under this clause. The limitation applies regardless of whether the claim sound in contract, tort, or otherwise.

facts.text: A material breach entitles the non-breaching party to terminate upon 30 days' written notice.
The non-breaching party may also pursue damages under Clause 12.
Injunctive relief is available without the 30-day notice requirement.
If the breaching party cures the breach within 15 days of the written notice, the non-breaching party may elect to continue the agreement on its existing terms.
An election to continue does not waive the right to claim damages for loss suffered during the breach period.
Neither party may pursue claims for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages under this clause, regardless of the legal basis of the claim.

forbidden_additions: A new remedy type not in the original.
A change to the 30-day notice or 15-day cure periods.
preserve: The 30-day notice for termination and Clause 12 damages reference.
The injunctive-relief exemption from the notice requirement.
The 15-day cure option and the election to continue.
The anti-waiver statement for damages during the breach period.
The exclusion of indirect, consequential, and punitive damages.
